opening.argument: The speaker claims he earned 40 Bitcoin by interacting with the BitConnect blockchain, emphasizing that he neither bought nor sold anything and that sign-up is free. He presents purported cash-outs of thousands of dollars every few days to support that claim. The on-screen steps then tell viewers to sign up at a website to be “Rich like me” and email him. That sequence turns an extraordinary account of easy earnings into a solicitation, rather than a neutral demonstration. The displayed balances and claimed withdrawals are presented as proof of wealth, but they do not establish that viewers will earn the same amount or that any particular outcome is guaranteed.

citations.quote: 40 bitcoin that I earned, I didn't buy. I earned this bitcoin with a service called BitConnect and I get paid to interact with the BitConnect blockchain.
I don't have to buy anything. I don't have to sell anything. And it's free to sign up.
